extracted.intended_audience: community college administrators and faculty preparing vocational education grant proposals (California Community Colleges)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for developing competitive technical and cost grant proposals for vocational education programs, tailored to respond to Requests for Proposals issued by California Community Colleges and similar public agencies. Covers planning, required proposal sections, budgeting, evaluation, dissemination, and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brainstorming and stakeholder input
rubrics_metrics.description: Brainstorm! Brainstorm! Brainstorm! Invite others to participate in a “brain dump” of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use group brainstorming to test, expand, and refine ideas and to gain support for the project (useful for obtaining administrative approval). Not all input will be used, but the process helps develop and strengthen the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break tasks into manageable pieces and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Break down the task into bite-size pieces. Do not try to write the proposal in one or two days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide work into smaller tasks; allow time for writing, rewriting, reflection, editing; make an outline and deadlines; determine research needs, assignment of sections, and internal deadlines to avoid panic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appropriate and documented references
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate and documented references to legislation, statistics, reports, relevant studies, past research, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure references are complete, accurate, and relevant to the current scope of work; put supporting data (enrollment, demographics) in appendices with pointer references in the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread and use outside editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread, Proofread, Proofread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an outside editor to review the final document for inconsistencies, clarifications, tone, grammar, syntax, typographical errors, and misspellings. Develop a final checklist to ensure nothing is omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand RFP types and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Know whether the solicitation is an RFP, RFQ, RFI, or RFA and the differing expectations for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFPs require detailed workscope, resumes, budget and timeline; RFQs focus on qualifications; RFIs are preliminary expressions of interest; RFAs ask all applicants to submit the same document as an RFP. Terms are sometimes used interchangeably—confirm expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere strictly to RFP format and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the instructions outlined in the RFP exactly as they are described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public agencies require specificity and standardization; failure to follow the format often results in disqualification. Exactly match titles, order, and required forms; submit the number of copies requested; sign originals where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop proposal in three parts (methodology, format, implementation plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing a response is a three part process: (1) create a response and sound methodology, (2) write sections according to required format and include supplemental info, (3) develop a realistic schemata for implementation if funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The implementation schemata should include realistic budget, timeframe, and identification of needed assistance (subcontractors, staffing). Each part is critical to a complete, realistic, and fundable proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required RFP sections in the technical proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the technical proposal contains the standard required sections such as needs statement, objectives, procedures/activities, project management, locations/facilities, evaluation, dissemination, project coordination, and statement of compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the RFP’s mandatory proposal format; cover page, abstract, table of contents, and appendices are standard. Respond to each required element fully and in the order requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret permissive vs directive language in RFPs (may vs shall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully search the RFP for words such as may and shall and interpret their meaning for required/optional tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘May’ is permissive and optional if you provide a strong rationale; ‘shall’ is directive and requires addressing the stated task. Use this to prioritize content and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualize project operation before writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptualize how you see the project in action—visualize operation once funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualization helps flesh out procedures/activities, staffing needs, timelines and realistic budgeting; it informs the rationale for activities and strengthens the proposal’s feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit support and research similar projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit support from others and research similar current or past projects to inform approach and learn from successes/failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage deans, administrators, faculty, students, and external providers; use findings and supporting documents (statistics, studies) to strengthen the needs statement and demonstrate prior knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose only work you can realistically implement
rubrics_metrics.description: Write what you can live with—the proposal will serve as primary implementation guide and may become contractual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only activities and final products you are confident you can deliver; avoid overpromising as you will be bound to implement listed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare realistic time estimates for proposal preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the time needed to prepare the proposal and set internal deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate time for each section based on available weeks before deadline; allocate time to writing, review, and compilation to stay on schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget by task before completing detailed budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a budget by each task including every cost associated with implementing the task before completing the detailed budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use spreadsheets to calculate hours and rates per task (example clerical hours), sum into line items, then enter totals into required budget forms to avoid miscalculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use internal approval and planning path
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a structured path (identify college approval process, research issues, identify need, brainstorm, set objectives and activities, determine costs and staffing, draft text, prepare spreadsheets, finalize budget and approvals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document provides a flowchart/checklist to track responsible persons, dates, and completion status; compile sections, obtain signatures, duplicate and send as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal completeness checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a checklist to ensure inclusion of Title Page, Abstract, Table of Contents, List of Figures, Needs Statement, Objectives, Procedures/Activities, Project Management, Project Coordination, Timeline, Location/Facilities, Evaluation, Dissemination, Statement of Compliance, Cost Proposal, Detailed Budget, Budget by Objective, and Appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track responsible person and due dates for each item; mark Completed/Not Applicable where appropriate. Missing components often lead to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover page requirements and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover page should be a concise letter to the contracting officer indicating who you are and what your proposal is about and must be signed by someone legally able to sign contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required identification number in the upper right-hand corner, signatures of district superintendent or authorized designee, chief administrator for occupational education, and project director if applicable. Some copies require original signatures—follow RFP instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content and length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If required, include an abstract that concisely summarizes the entire proposal in less than 500 words and cannot exceed the space provided on the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract must include statements on objectives, procedures, expected contribution/impact, and resulting products/services. Keep it concise and strictly within provided space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents and pagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a separate Table of Contents, number all pages at the bottom, and indicate page numbers for each narrative component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing tables/figures is optional; appendices need not be listed. Ensure TOC matches section titles exactly as in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs Statement clarity and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Introduction/Needs Statement must concisely state the need to be addressed, how the proposal will improve the situation, and how it maps to the grant objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the needs statement: leads the reader to conclude funding is warranted; fits within grant scope; shows research (state/local studies, stats); presents substantiating facts; describes local specifics (not only statewide generalities); describes target group; anticipates results; ends with a strong summarizing sentence. Put supporting data in appendices and reference them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-formed goals and measurable objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State goals (overall intent) and objectives (specific measurable outcomes). Number all objectives and state them in measurable terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should demonstrate how they promote progress in vocational education and improve programs/services. For research/curriculum projects, demonstrate a reasonable probability that results will be used in a substantial number of classrooms within five years. Ask 'How will I know when I have achieved my objective?' for each objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures/Activities aligned to objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe procedures and activities that will be used to accomplish each objective, including sequence and timeline narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain rationale for selecting each activity and show logical links between objectives and activities. Avoid activities that do not tie to objectives and ensure every objective has corresponding activities. Use charts to map objectives to activities where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline realism and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline showing the relationship between procedures/activities and the project calendar, indicating sequential and concurrent activities and staff involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show when activities will be ahead/on/behind schedule, amount of time/staff devoted to major activities, and allow realistic time for events outside control. Build in slack; use simple tools if needed; use line styles or color to add detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project management plan and staffing commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a management plan describing operation of the project, evidence of staff commitment, roles, and time commitments for named individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why individuals were selected (talents, expertise), how team members will work together, and how they will work with the contracting agency. Include brief bios/resumes relevant to the project (only include experience directly related to the proposal) and an organizational chart when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use strong action verbs and avoid weak resume language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use strong words (e.g., Managed, Developed, Coordinated) in resumes and project descriptions and avoid weak phrases (e.g., Assisted, Participated in, Helped with).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provided list shows words to use (e.g., Evaluated, Researched, Facilitated, Generated) and words to avoid. Tailor resume language to emphasize relevant accomplishments and leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locations and facilities relevance and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify project headquarters, sites, and locations of activities and show evidence that facilities are available when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how locations/facilities were selected and why; include relevant campus resources (conference rooms, labs, computer capabilities) and staff availability; include only facilities information directly relevant to the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan (formative, summative, and third-party)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how you will determine whether the project met its objectives using in-house formative and summative evaluation methods and methods for treating evaluation data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate 5–15% of total direct costs for an independent third-party evaluation (subject to RFP limits). Use measurable objectives as the starting point to develop indicators and an evaluation plan tailored to those objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination plan and sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a plan for working with agencies and individuals who would benefit, outline methods/extent of dissemination, and describe how outcomes will be presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for dissemination activities and discuss which aspects of the project will be continued or replicated after the initial project. Note: omission of evaluation or dissemination plans can lead to disqualification in Chancellor’s Office projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Compliance completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Read, complete and sign the Statement of Compliance form included with the RFP (required by the State General Services Department).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the compliance form is included and signed; failure to include required forms may disqualify the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appendices for supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Place supporting, secondary, or auxiliary material in the Appendices (letters of commitment, enrollment data, maps, sample materials, legislation, meeting minutes, bibliographies, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interrupt the main narrative with bulky documents. When in doubt, put it in the Appendices. Experienced grant writers advise: better to have a concise proposal and fat appendices than the reverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost proposal must be reasonable and within maximum funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost/Price bid must be reasonable and must be in a total amount equal to or less than the maximum funding designated in the RFP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public agencies may award funds to the lowest qualified bidder. Prepare a Budget Summary for each funding source, Budget by Objective, and a Detailed Budget using RFP budget forms. Failure to complete required budget forms will result in proposals not being reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed budget line-item justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed budget with line item breakdowns (salaries, indirect costs, books, printing, etc.) and calculate costs by task before entering line item totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate hours and rates for each task and category (e.g., clerical hours), sum to totals for line items (e.g., line 2100 clerical), and ensure consistency between the budget spreadsheet and required forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project budget by objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Transpose each objective onto the Project-by-Objective form and break down anticipated expenses by objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows the funding agency which objectives will absorb the bulk of funds and demonstrates alignment between objectives and resource allocation; spreadsheet software is ideal for this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project budget summary and matching funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete a Project Budget Summary for each funding source and report matching funds where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure matching funds meet RFP requirements and are clearly identified on the summary form; follow any restrictions (indirect cost limits, caps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall coherence and feasibility check (Tying It All Together)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the sum of the parts equals the whole and that sections contribute unique but interlinking information showing how the project meets objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check logical connections, tone consistency, answer What/Where/When/Why/Who/How, evaluate doability (timeframe, qualified staff, realistic activities, plausible costs), identify unresolved questions or environmental limitations, confirm abstract relates to central proposal, and trim nonessential material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide road maps, clearly label sections identical to the Table of Contents, and use readable type and margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use strong verbs, bullets for brief points, visual elements (tables/charts/figures) sparingly and purposefully, prefer shorter sentences and paragraphs, summarize and highlight key points, use numbering/lists when appropriate, and exactly match proposal sections to the RFP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission and signature logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit as many copies of the proposal as directed and ensure required signatures and originals on some copies where specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check RFP for number of copies, signature requirements, deadlines, bidder workshops, and any calendar of important dates; missing or incorrectly executed submission logistics can disqualify proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include dissemination and evaluation budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the budget reflects costs for both evaluation activities and dissemination efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since evaluation and dissemination are frequently required components, the budget should include line items for independent evaluation and dissemination activities (printing, duplication, travel, workshops).
